# Getting started with Local Development

# Environment

-   Latest version of [NVM](https://github.com/nvm-sh/nvm)

-   Latest version of [AWS CLI](https://aws.amazon.com/cli/)

-   Assigned AWS accounts and IAM credentials
-   [Redoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc#redoc-cli) for automatically generating html from the open api specification, see install [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/25800493/converting-swagger-specification-json-to-html-documentation)

-   Latest version of [Helm](https://helm.sh/) see the install guild [here](https://helm.sh/docs/intro/install/)

For the remainng item of this list, you should figure out yourself if you don't already know.

-   [Git](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Getting-Started-Installing-Git)
-   A good terminal (such as [iTerm2](https://iterm2.com/index.html) + [ohmyzsh](https://ohmyz.sh/))
-   A good IDE (such as [VSCode](https://code.visualstudio.com/), or [WebStorm](https://www.jetbrains.com/webstorm/))

# Setup

1. Configure AWS CLI. `aws configure`. See sample config below. Use _us-east-1_ as default region and _json_ as default output format.

```bash
aws configure
AWS Access Key ID [None]: XXXXXXXXXXX
AWS Secret Access Key [None]: XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX
Default region name [None]: us-east-1
Default output format [None]: json
```

2. Clone the repository.
3. Run: `npm run setup:influx` Visit _http://localhost:8086_ to make sure InfluxDB is running locally.
4. Going through the setup guide of local InfuxDB. Configure the `local-usage-data` bucket, the `local-config` bucket and the `metering` org. **Case sensitive**.

The implementation is complete. Summary of the changes:

**Problem**: The invoicing collector (`InvoiceLineGathererService` → `Offering.getLineItemsForUsage`) charged every unit of aggregated usage for non-tiered dimensions, ignoring the billing catalogue's allowances (`usageEntitlement`) and overage rules (`overageAllowed`), and it emitted a line for every dimension regardless of whether anything was owed or whether the invoice settings hide free dimensions.

**Fix** in `src/offering/entities/offeringPackage.entity.ts`:

1. Added `Offering.chargeableTotal({ total, usageEntitlement, overageAllowed })`:
   - no allowance → every unit is chargeable;
   - `inf` allowance → nothing chargeable;
   - plan forbids overage (anything other than `overageAllowed: 'true'`) → nothing chargeable;
   - finite allowance → only the exhausted excess `usage - allowance` (never negative).
2. The non-tiered dimension totals now hold that chargeable amount, so invoice quantities reflect only permitted overage.
3. Line emission rules: a dimension gets a line when the customer owes something on it (chargeable usage > 0 at a non-zero unit cost), and a dimension the plan prices at zero (including a missing/zero `consumptionPrice`) gets a line unless `settings.freeDimensionOnInvoice === hide`; otherwise it is skipped.

**Verified against the local AWS-compatible emulator** (catalogues in `metering-billing-sandbox`, usage in the `Metering/Usage` CloudWatch namespace):
- `biz-ridge` (hide free dimensions): alpha → API Calls 100@0.01 and Seats 2@10 (12 used of a 10 allowance with overage allowed); the zero-priced Alerts, the overage-forbidden Reports and the unlimited Storage produce no lines. bravo → only Jobs 200@0.05 (unexhausted Minutes, unlimited Scans, overage-forbidden Tasks all drop out).
- `biz-vale` (show free dimensions): Messages 50@0.01, free Hours 10@0, Units 5@5.

Plus a new unit spec `src/offering/entities/allowanceLineItems.spec.ts` covering the allowance/overage matrix and show/hide behaviour; the existing unit suite still passes (the only failures are pre-existing, network-dependent ones), lint is clean and no new type errors were introduced.
